verdict.rationale: Rive documents exporting files for its runtimes, and those runtimes are open-source libraries that can load .riv files. RML gives an XML text representation of a Rive file, which offers a partial open-format route. Community users report there is no way to export movie files, and the open-source part is only the runtime, which still needs the Rive Editor to build content. missing for 10: documented full-account/all-data export, evidence that the .riv format is an openly specified standard, a documented editor-to-RML export path, export to common interchange formats (e.g. video, SVG), independent corroboration of leaving without lock-in.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: You can use the same exported file across supported runtimes, including web, mobile, game engines, and other platforms.
The Rive runtimes are open-source libraries that allow you to load and control your animations in apps, games, and websites.
Rive Markup Language (RML) is a text-based representation of a Rive file.
RML uses XML to describe the objects and relationships in a Rive file
